They are not a matched pair of safety and non-safety bargaining-unit contracts: the ordinance expressly states that the Chief of Police had been removed from the police bargaining unit, and the administrative-assistant provision is a municipal position rate.
caveats: The defensible comparison window is January 1-June 30, 2018, not the entire 2018-2021 police award cycle.

The non-safety side is an Administrative Assistant position rate, not a separately verified non-safety bargaining-unit contract record.
Role, rank, duties, work schedule, full-time status, and hours equivalence are not established.
The 199.2% figure is an arithmetic contrast between two documented position rates and must not be interpreted as an Alburtis bargaining-unit wage-gap estimate.
Manual/legal/substantive review is required before any analytic use beyond an appendix-level documentary illustration.
why_usable_or_not: The exact values, hourly basis, regular/base character, and overlapping January-June 2018 period are source-grounded, and the arithmetic is correct. The comparison is usable only as a heavily qualified local documentary position-rate illustration because it does not satisfy the project's matched bargaining-unit unit of observation and lacks role/rank/hours comparability.
bounded_pi_report_statement: Alburtis Ordinance No. 546 provides bounded local documentary evidence that, during the overlapping January-June 2018 window, the Chief of Police rate was $33.57 per hour and the Administrative Assistant rate was $11.22 per hour. On the current normalized basis, the arithmetic difference is $22.35 per hour, or 199.2% relative to the administrative-assistant rate. This is a current source-grounded comparison of two municipal position rates—not a final wage-gap estimate or a matched bargaining-unit comparison—and it is not nationally representative; the Chief's exclusion from the bargaining unit and unresolved role, schedule, hours, and position equivalence require manual/legal/substantive validation before analytic use.
pi_report_one_sentence: Alburtis Ordinance No. 546 supplies bounded local documentary evidence that the Chief of Police rate ($33.57/hour) exceeded the Administrative Assistant rate ($11.22/hour) by $22.35/hour, or 199.2%, during their overlapping January-June 2018 window, but this is a position-rate illustration requiring manual validation—not a final wage-gap estimate or matched bargaining-unit comparison.
pi_report_two_to_three_sentence: For January through June 2018, Alburtis Ordinance No. 546 records a $33.57 hourly rate for the Chief of Police and an $11.22 hourly rate for the Administrative Assistant. On the current normalized basis, that is a $22.35 hourly arithmetic difference, or 199.2% relative to the administrative-assistant rate. The ordinance also states that the Chief had been removed from the police bargaining unit, so this bounded local documentary evidence belongs only in a limits or appendix discussion unless manual/legal/substantive review establishes a defensible analytic use; it is not a final wage-gap estimate and is not nationally representative.
table_ready_version: Alburtis, PA | Jan-Jun 2018 | Chief of Police $33.57/hr | Administrative Assistant $11.22/hr | +$22.35/hr (+199.2%) | conditional documentary position-rate comparison; not matched bargaining units
caveat_text: Same ordinance and overlapping period, but not matched bargaining-unit contracts: the Chief was outside the police bargaining unit, and role/rank/hours/schedule equivalence with the Administrative Assistant is unverified. Use only as bounded local documentary evidence after manual/legal/substantive validation, not as a final wage-gap estimate.
forbidden_claim_warning: Do not state that the Alburtis wage gap is 199.2%, that safety workers in Alburtis generally earned 199.2% more, that the comparison is representative, or that bargaining caused the difference. The evidence supports only a bounded, January-June 2018 documentary contrast between the named positions.
